answer: Iterated-seed uniqueness gate: each applicant submits a fresh random seed, and the registry derives their ID as a slow, memory-hard hash whose output curves over a fixed ridge of precomputed checkpoints. A second pass runs the same seed through a mirror hash and requires the two results to agree on a hidden cipher pattern only valid seeds satisfy. Enforcement: only one ID per seed, and reusing any earlier seed is rejected. An attacker farming N identities must generate N distinct valid seeds and pay N full hash chains, so marginal cost per identity stays flat and large.
